heading: Classic 'polysemantic' neurons, like InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron, detect one feature their categories share
definition: classic examples such as InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron detect a coherent shared feature (a V or bilateral pointed shape), a pattern the essay calls recursive generalization, not superposition.
summary: Only the original essay reports this reading, from its author's own inspection of one neuron and one circuit, with no blind check (one where the rater does not know the expected answer). No independent study supports or challenges it; one study of a different InceptionV1 neuron found mixed results, depending on the strength of an L1 sparsity penalty, that point toward superposition (features sharing neurons).

suggested_status.by_scale: R0 at <1B: InceptionV1 (7.06M parameters per original R10), original only. Not tested in toy models, at 1-10B, 10-100B or >100B, or in any language model. counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size {not stated: 3, <1B: 1}.
suggested_status.reason: Only the original reports the reading: one neuron (4e:55, R10) and one circuit (car-to-dog, R11), read by its author without a stated method or a blind check. counts: versions.V3.verdicts.supports.studies 0; versions.V3.verdicts.challenges.studies 0; versions.V3.verdicts.limits_scope.studies 1. That one study is arXiv:2406.03662, which tests a different InceptionV1 neuron with mixed, L1-dependent results that the verdict reads as pointing to superposition. counts: versions.V3.studies_tested_without_verdict 1 (arXiv:1602.03616, CaffeNet, cannot_determine rows); versions.V3.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original 0; versions.V3.main_rows_by_operation {measurement: 6}, with no causal rows.
suggested_status.open_questions: The level would rise to R2 if a different group re-examined InceptionV1 4e:55 or the car-to-dog circuit (SAE or dictionary decomposition across L1 values, ablation, blind multi-rater labels) and found the shared shape/pose reading. It would move to C if 4e:55 split cleanly into separate cat and car features. Also open: whether the essay's language-model example (the Towards Monosemanticity mixture neuron) holds, and what share of canonical polysemantic neurons resolve this way.

original_result.setup: The author re-reads InceptionV1 neurons using their top images, feature visualizations, the neurons that feed into them and that read from them, and their negative sides.
original_result.result: Neuron 4e:55, once read as a mix of cats and cars, responds to a V or bilateral pointed shape that both share, and its negative side responds to round shapes. Of four neurons that read from car neuron 4c:447, visualized with guidance from natural images, two are car neurons and two respond to a pose shared by cars and dogs, which unguided visualization had drawn as dogs.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: InceptionV1's double-curve neuron split mostly into single-curve SAE features, depending on sparsity.

wording_issues.issue: arXiv:2406.03662 decomposes InceptionV1 neurons with branch-specific SAEs. Only mixed3b/n/359, a double-curve neuron, is in rows. At the default L1 it splits mainly into two single-curve features plus a residual double-curve feature (R4, partial; following the verdict's correction of the row). The verdict reads this as pointing to superposition (limits_scope). In two extra SAEs with higher L1 (values not stated), the double-curve feature becomes smaller (R5). The neuron therefore splits into parts at every tested L1, and L1 changes only the size of the residual double-curve feature. Section 3.1 of the same study (not in rows) also decomposes two more neurons. The first is conv2d1/n/44, which Olah et al. 2020 could not categorise; it splits into brightness-gradient, colour-contrast and complex Gabor features. The second is mixed3b/n/376, a boundary detector that prefers fur; it splits into a generic boundary feature and a fur-specific one. None of these neurons is 4e:55, so the study does not test the cat-and-car neuron.

The rows behind the reading cover one neuron and one circuit, both read by the essay's author (R10 note: one neuron, one reader, no blind reading; R11 note: pose-neuron count given without a method). The essay's other re-read example, the Towards Monosemanticity mixture neuron, is not in rows. In CaffeNet, arXiv:1602.03616's own reading of fc6 unit 22 (fires for turtles, scuba …) is cannot_determine (R1). Its authors also state, outside the rows, that many fc6/fc7 units seem to represent an amalgam, while fc8 class units are purer.

method_sensitivity.what: For InceptionV1 mixed3b/n/359, the default SAE (lambda 3.5e-6 for mixed3b, 8x expansion, trained on the 5x5 branch only; Table 1) splits the neuron mainly into two single-curve features plus one double-curve feature (R4). Two extra SAEs with higher L1 coefficients (values not given) lower the double-curve feature's maximum activation and raise that of the left- and right-curve features (R5). The text says the double-curve feature becomes smaller, not that it disappears. The author ran the higher-L1 SAEs to check whether the double-curve feature is an SAE failure. L1 changes the size of the residual double-curve feature. No tested setting shows the neuron as one coherent feature, so the reading does not switch between coherent and superposed.

For the InceptionV1 car-to-dog circuit, free optimization of the car neuron's readers drew dogs. Optimization guided along natural-image paths showed two of four readers to be car neurons and two sharing a feature the essay calls pose (R11). The original reports this; no other study re-runs it.

method_sensitivity.factor: Evidence used to read a neuron (top-k examples vs negative pole, circuits, thresholds)
method_sensitivity.what: The original states that top-k examples alone can mislead (it names the negative pole and long context among the reasons). It also says its percentages depend on where the threshold for 'one thing' is set. Its 4e:55 reading draws on image grids, circuit connections to flames and fireboat water jets, and the negative pole, an O (R10).

method_sensitivity.factor: Facet clustering (k in k-means) and initialization in multifaceted visualization
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:1602.03616 notes that the number of facets depends on the chosen k, and that different starting images can converge to similar visualizations. For CaffeNet fc6 unit 461, visualizations initialized from the mean images of different facets converged to a similar hybrid image (R2, cannot_determine; verdict correction moves the locator to Supplementary S3, Fig. S5c right). For fc6 unit 22, facets were formed with k=10 from the top 1000 validation images (R1).
